analysis.title: Uber Technologies Inc. (UBER) Q3'26 Earnings Review: Solid Quarter & Forward Guide Punctuated by AV Strategy Update and Anchoring Around key Themes of Secular Growth & Capital Allocation
key_insights: GS reiterates Buy on UBER and keeps the 12-month price target at $110 against a $69.87 price (57.4% upside) after updating estimates for Q3'26 results and management's forward commentary.
At about $70, UBER trades at 16x GS 2027 non-GAAP EPS, which GS expects to grow at a 30% 2025-2028 CAGR to about $5.50, and at 11x equity/(FCF-SBC) on 2027 estimates.
Management now expects driverless vehicles on the platform to scale from 700 at YE 2026 to 2,000 by YE 2027, and gave more detail on learnings from current AV operations.
Q3'26 Mobility gross bookings were $29,512mm, 2% below GS ($30,230mm) and 1% below consensus ($29,890mm). Mobility revenue was $7,520mm, 3% below GS and 2% below consensus.

Management said international Mobility growth was hurt by supply constraints in a select number of countries, tied to elevated fuel costs, local labor conditions and competition for drivers. Overall Mobility growth trends improved in October.
Delivery gross bookings grew 23% YoY, driven by record frequency (helped by Uber One and merchant investments). Grocery & Retail gross bookings grew about 40% YoY.
Merchant spending on advertising and offers in Delivery has passed a $10bn annualized run rate.
Freight beat by a wide margin: gross bookings $1,768mm vs GS $1,307mm (+35%) and consensus $1,491mm (+19%).

Adjusted EBITDA of $2,963mm was 2% above GS and 1% above consensus, within the $2.86-2.96bn guide range. Margin was 5.0% of gross bookings, 12bps above GS. Non-GAAP EPS was $0.88 vs GS $0.86 and consensus $0.86.
Monthly active platform consumers hit a record 215mm (+14% YoY) and monthly frequency rose 2%. U4B grew +50%.

Management expects Q4 take rates to be hit by higher driver activation and retention spending to improve supply. The Middle East conflict cost 75bps of Q3 Mobility gross bookings growth, and the Q4 outlook assumes a 100bps headwind.

GS cut Q4'26 gross bookings to $64.68bn (from $65.08bn) and non-GAAP EPS to $0.97 (from $0.98). It raised 2027 gross bookings to $279.95bn (from $274.23bn) and trimmed 2027 non-GAAP EPS to $4.33 (from $4.35).
GS cut its EV/GAAP EBITDA target multiple to 18.0x from 19.0x to hold a growth-adjusted multiple near 0.7x. The 15.0x EV/FCF-SBC multiple and 12% discount rate are unchanged.

market_movers.rationale: GS keeps Buy and the $110 target after Q3'26. It cites AV scaling, Delivery strength and a 30% 2025-2028 EPS CAGR, and lowers the EBITDA multiple to 18.0x from 19.0x.

earnings_insights: UBER Q3'26 reported 11/4 (GS note): non-GAAP EPS $0.88 vs GS est $0.86 and consensus est $0.86, within company guide of $0.84-0.88.
UBER Q3'26 reported adj. EBITDA $2,963mm vs GS est $2,901mm and consensus est $2,921mm, guide $2.86-2.96bn. Margin 5.0% of gross bookings vs GS est 4.8%.
UBER Q3'26 reported gross bookings $59,819mm vs GS est $60,006mm and consensus est $59,830mm, guide $58.25-60.25bn. Revenue $14,766mm vs GS est $14,580mm and consensus est $14,673mm.

Q3'26 Mobility gross bookings $29,512mm reported vs GS est $30,230mm and consensus est $29,890mm. Delivery $28,539mm vs GS est $28,469mm and consensus est $28,392mm. Freight $1,768mm vs GS est $1,307mm and consensus est $1,491mm.
GS new estimates: Q4'26E non-GAAP EPS $0.97 (old $0.98), gross bookings $64.68bn, revenue $15.49bn. 2027E non-GAAP EPS $4.33 (old $4.35), 2028E $5.48 (old $5.61), 2029E $6.54 (old $6.79).
Management guided that Q4 take rates will be pressured by driver activation and retention investment. GS cut its Q4'26E Mobility take rate to 24.4% from 25.0%.
risk_factors: Slower Mobility growth from demand elasticity, maturation and competition from autonomous vehicles.
Driver classification rules (compensation, benefits), merchant commission caps and ESG regulation.
Competition in Mobility and Delivery, including local commerce and logistics.
Normalization of consumer discretionary spending habits in Delivery.
Volatility from the global macro environment and investor risk appetite for growth stocks.
Supply constraints in international Mobility from fuel costs, labor conditions and driver competition.
geopolitical: The ongoing Middle East conflict cost 75bps of Q3 Mobility gross bookings growth. Management's outlook assumes a 100bps headwind in Q4.
